bug_semantics: networkstatus_parse_detached_signatures and networkstatus_parse_vote_from_string accept any digest name crypto_digest_algorithm_parse_name understands (sha1=0, sha256=1, sha512=2, sha3-256=3, sha3-512=4) after only testing a<0, then use that digest_algorithm_t as an index into common_digests_t.d[N_COMMON_DIGEST_ALGORITHMS][DIGEST256_LEN] where N_COMMON_DIGEST_ALGORITHMS is DIGEST_SHA256+1 (two slots). An additional-digest line with alg sha3-256/sha512/sha3-512 therefore does an out-of-bounds write through base16_decode(digests->d[alg], ...) plus an OOB read in tor_mem_is_zero/fast_mem_is_zero(digests->d[alg], ...); a consensus directory-signature with an unexpected Algorithm stores sig->alg and later networkstatus_check_document_signature OOB-reads consensus->digests.d[sig->alg]. Unauthenticated consensus or detached-signature documents can trigger it (CWE-787). Impact is minor for most Tor roles and potentially major for directory authorities (TROVE-2026-019 / tor#41267).
flaw_origin: The additional-digest parser has indexed d[alg] from parse_name since 0.2.2.6-alpha (5576a3a094de49246e501bb24d1b3dc3a5d610b9, 2009), when the digest array still covered every parse_name result. SHA512 (ff54cc8481f88ecbc40a8abc0a1812fcf583ea73) and SHA3 (687f9b3bd7b55bcf4d984d745e978c2a03aeb4e1) grew N_DIGEST_ALGORITHMS and the array together, so d[alg] stayed in-bounds. 39b597c2fd8b45ff61573c70c36e8a4846cf3a0e (ticket 17795) then shrank digests_t from d[N_DIGEST_ALGORITHMS][DIGEST512_LEN] to d[N_COMMON_DIGEST_ALGORITHMS][DIGEST256_LEN] without tightening the directory parsers' a<0-only checks, first creating the parse_name versus N_COMMON mismatch. That is the smallest public commit whose parent still has an in-bounds array for every parse_name value; it first appears in tor-0.2.8.2-alpha, matching the vendor bugfix-on line.

crypto_digest.h at fix parent: DIGEST_SHA1=0, SHA256=1, SHA512=2, SHA3_256=3, SHA3_512=4; N_COMMON_DIGEST_ALGORITHMS=(DIGEST_SHA256+1)=2; common_digests_t.d[2][DIGEST256_LEN]. crypto_digest_algorithm_parse_name returns those five names or -1. reasoning: CVE-2026-77642 is a published CWE-787 (not withdrawn/rejected). The exploitable mechanism is indexing common_digests_t.d[] with a crypto_digest_algorithm_parse_name result that can be SHA512/SHA3 after only rejecting a<0. That array is sized N_COMMON_DIGEST_ALGORITHMS (SHA1+SHA256 only). Detached-signature additional-digest is an OOB write during parse; consensus directory-signature with an unexpected Algorithm is an OOB read during signature check. Directory authorities parse detached signatures, which is why impact is 'potentially major' there. The 2026 fix (49565af98e44001cf4611253b558cb1f22587347) only adds a>=N_COMMON_DIGEST_ALGORITHMS at the three parse_name sites; vendor changelog attributes the bug to 0.2.8.2-alpha. The 2009 additional-digest parser (5576a3a09, first in 0.2.2.6-alpha) first wrote the d[alg] lines, but at that time and through 0.2.8.1-alpha the digest array grew with N_DIGEST_ALGORITHMS so every parse_name value stayed in-bounds (confirmed by the 39b597c2 parent diff still using d[N_DIGEST_ALGORITHMS][DIGEST512_LEN] while SHA512/SHA3 already existed). The smallest commit that first created the OOB is therefore 39b597c2fd8b45ff61573c70c36e8a4846cf3a0e, which introduced N_COMMON and shrank the array without updating the parsers. Immediate parent 4770db8e992365c12c652f53a7d3fd84bae25bcb is a real commit (in 0.2.8.1-alpha) whose tree is not OOB for this path; 39b597c2 is not a merge, move, revert, or squash. Follow-ups 8a4bba06d (rename) and 94c8f3605 (dirvote N_DIGEST loops) did not write the parser mismatch. 2018 file splits are moves, not BICs. BIC commit-object identity is Nick Mathewson 2016 with no AI trailers, so verdict is NOT_AI. Fix SHA is the bounds-check commit, present in tor-0.4.9.9 and absent from tor-0.4.9.8.
